This guide will walk you through deploying your digital commerce stack, ensuring that you can accept [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/tron-usdt-payments-digital-products-first-principles-definitive-2|COREMERCH guide to payments]] and deliver products seamlessly.

content.text: Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail

Traditional payment platforms often exclude creators in Ghana, leaving them unable to access essential financial tools. Blockchain technology, however, provides an alternative that is both efficient and inclusive. By utilizing cryptocurrencies like USDT on Tron, which settles transactions in under 60 seconds for a fee of less than $0.10, you can facilitate quick and cost-effective payments. This infrastructure not only empowers you but also ensures that you retain full ownership of your data and operations.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Before deploying your digital commerce stack, gather the necessary tools. You will need a GitHub or Cloudflare account for hosting, a Google account for backend integration, and a NOWPayments account to manage cryptocurrency transactions. Familiarize yourself with the platforms, as the Sovereign Starter Stack or Edge Commerce Stack will require you to set up product listings and payment information. Ensure you have your product files ready to upload for immediate delivery once a sale is completed.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

Start by deploying your chosen stack. If you opt for the Sovereign Starter Stack, use GitHub Pages combined with Google Apps Script for backend functionality. This setup allows you to create a seamless product delivery pipeline. Integrate NOWPayments for automatic crypto payment processing. Upon payment confirmation, your product files will be delivered directly to customers. This automation streamlines operations, significantly reducing the time and effort needed to manage transactions.
Blockchain payments eliminate geographic barriers for creators.
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

Once your stack is deployed and configured, it's time to go live. Share your store link on social media and other platforms to attract buyers. Monitor your NOWPayments dashboard to track incoming transactions. When a customer makes a purchase, the payment will be processed, and the product will be delivered automatically. This real-time transaction processing ensures you can focus on creating while your infrastructure handles the sales.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

After successfully processing initial transactions, consider scaling your operations. Expand your product offerings by adding more digital items to your store. Utilize the Complete Builder Kit to access advanced templates and blueprints which can enhance your store's functionality. Engage with your audience through marketing strategies that promote your brand. As your sales grow, your infrastructure will support increased traffic and transaction volume without additional costs.
How can creators in Africa sell digital products to international buyers?

Global access through sovereign infrastructure works because every layer of the stack is geography-neutral by design. Cloudflare Pages serves your storefront from data centers close to your buyer — whether they are in London or Lagos, the page loads in under 200 milliseconds. NOWPayments generates a unique payment address for each transaction — the buyer sends crypto from any wallet, anywhere in the world. The blockchain confirms the transaction regardless of which country the sender is in. Your Cloudflare Worker receives the webhook and processes the order using the same logic for every buyer.
You retain complete ownership of your digital commerce infrastructure.
Related: How Creators Like You Are Building Sovereign Stores

Global access to digital product revenue is not contingent on where you are located — it is contingent on which infrastructure you build on. The sovereign stack works identically from Lagos, Accra, Nairobi, Karachi, Dhaka, Harare, or Manila. The Edge Commerce Stack at $197 is deployed by COREMERCH in 48 hours under your accounts, tested on mainnet before handoff. The Sovereign Blueprint at $47 documents the complete build for self-deployers. Both are available at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html.
Your Deployment Checklist

Open a self-custody wallet — Trust Wallet or MetaMask — and back up the seed phrase before configuring anything else. Create your NOWPayments account and configure the self-custody wallet addresses as your payout destination. Open a Binance account and complete enough P2P setup to verify you can convert USDT to your local currency. Deploy your stack and configure the NOWPayments webhook endpoint. Build your product pages with USD prices and confirm the checkout generates QR codes and live price feeds correctly. Run a mainnet test transaction from a second wallet to confirm the full pipeline. Do a test P2P conversion with a small amount of USDT to confirm the conversion process works end-to-end. Promote your store.
Frequently Asked Questions
What cryptocurrency options can I use for payments?

NOWPayments supports over 300 cryptocurrencies, allowing you to choose the best options for your audience. Popular choices include USDT and Bitcoin, which provide flexibility and lower transaction fees.
How do I deliver products to customers after payment?
After integrating NOWPayments with your store, product delivery is automated. Upon payment confirmation, customers receive their purchased digital products via email or a direct download link.
Can I scale my operations easily?

Yes, once your infrastructure is in place, scaling is straightforward. You can add new products and leverage the Complete Builder Kit to enhance your store's capabilities without significant additional effort.
What if I encounter technical issues during setup?
You can access 30-day support with the Sovereign Starter Stack or Edge Commerce Stack. Utilize community forums and documentation for troubleshooting assistance.
Is there a way to accept payments in local currencies?
Yes, Binance P2P supports local currencies like naira, cedis, Kenyan shillings, and Pakistani rupees, allowing you to facilitate transactions that cater to your audience's preferences.
